subject: Renewal pricing & risk-sharing proposal
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@crowdstitch.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@crowdstitch.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal pricing: renewal window and cost pressure

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. We're reaching the end of our annual term and I need to pull together a recommendation for our CFO and procurement team. Two key things from our side:

- Usage has been up ~45% YoY in Q1 and Q2 (see attached usage export).
- We need pricing predictability for the next 12 months — our engineering + GTM forecasts assume a stable unit cost while we ramp a new feature set.

Procurement asked whether Redwood can:
1) hold current unit pricing for at least 9 months,
2) provide a modest uplift in committed capacity with a step-up discount, and
3) offer a one-time onboarding/migration credit to offset migration/testing bursts.

If you can put together a concrete offer (numbers and triggers), I can run it with finance and loop in legal. We also have a preferred e-sign flow to speed execution.

Attachment: crowdstitch_usage_q1_q2.xlsx

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Partnerships
CrowdStitch
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@crowdstitch.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing: renewal window and cost pressure

Elena — appreciate the context and the export. We can get you something tightly scoped. High-level proposal for internal review and to share with your CFO/procurement:

1) Term & commit
- 12-month renewal.
- 20% increase to committed tokens in year 1 (applies to generation + embed units).

2) Price stability / hold
- 10% price hold (unit price unchanged) for the first 9 months of the renewal.
- After month 9, unit price can step up at a pre-agreed schedule tied to actual average monthly consumption (we'll include a cap).

3) Credits & onboarding
- One-time $75,000 onboarding/migration credit applied against the first invoice.
- $25k of that is escrowed and released after performance checklist (canary run) completes.

4) Risk-sharing clause (new) — to address your volatility
- If monthly usage exceeds committed tier by >30% for 2 consecutive months, Redwood will apply a temporary burst multiplier instead of immediate overage billing for up to 60 days while we jointly rebaseline.
- If sustained overage persists beyond the 60-day window, standard overage rates apply.

5) SLAs & offsets
- 99.9% availability SLA for production routes in the Dedicated pool; service credits for outages beyond SLA.

I'll attach our internal commit options doc so you can see the pricing ladders and examples. If this looks ok in principle, we can: (a) confirm the pricing grid (laura), (b) lock the legal language (marissa + your legal), and (c) prepare a DocuSign for expedited signing.

Attachments: redwood_commit_options.pdf

Action items:
- Elena: confirm whether the 20% commit uplift is acceptable to finance.
- Procurement (cc): confirm e-sign process or invite your counterparty.
- Laura: I'll need a pricing grid with the 9-month hold and the step-up cap by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: I'll need a short risk-sharing amendment we can attach to the SOW.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@crowdstitch.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@crowdstitch.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing: renewal window and cost pressure

Karthik — thanks, that structure is sensible and closer to what finance wants. A few clarifications from procurement/legal:

- We need explicit language for the "price hold" (start/end dates) and the formula for the step-up cap.
- The escrow release conditions for the $25k need to be defined (suggest: canary passes + one week of stable error rates).
- Can you provide the SLA credit schedule? Procurement will want thresholds spelled out.

Procurement is ready to accept a DocuSign link for the commercial terms and prefers a single amendment that sits alongside the existing Master Services Agreement. I'll attach the procurement checklist they want completed before countersigning.

Attachment: procurement_terms_crowdstitch.pdf

If you can get legal language and a doc ready by Friday, we'll prioritize review and aim to sign next week.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Partnerships
CrowdStitch
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-08T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: CrowdStitch renewal — confirm final commercials and docs (ST-3247)

Laura / Marissa — looping you back in with Elena's procurement ask. Summary + asks:

Summary of the agreed commercial direction (high level):
- 12-month renewal, 20% committed uplift in year 1.
- 9-month 10% price hold, then pre-agreed step-up schedule (cap at +6% per quarter; cap floor TBD).
- $75k onboarding credit (apply to invoice 1); $25k held in escrow and released after canary criteria.
- Risk-sharing: temporary burst multipliers for 60 days before overage billing kicks in.
- 99.9% SLA with credit table to include in amendment.

Asks:
1) Laura — please confirm the attached pricing grid that maps committed tiers to unit price and includes the 9-month hold + step-up cap. Need this as a table we can drop into the amendment. Deadline: tomorrow EOD.
2) Marissa — please draft a short amendment and SOW addendum that includes: price hold wording with explicit start/end, escrow release conditions (canary pass + 7d stability), SLA credit table, and the risk-sharing paragraph. Keep it scoped so legal can turn quickly. Deadline: Friday COB.
3) I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope once we have the pricing grid + amendment.

Related links: https://redwood.app/plays/commit-options/ST-3247 (pricing examples)
DocuSign placeholder: https://app.docusign.com/abcdef123456789

If we can get these three items aligned, Elena said procurement will prioritize and they hope to sign next week. This motion is a good reference for a fast-track renewal play — recommend we record the final grid in the deal playbook after close.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
